content.content:
1	---
2	name: proof-kit
3	description: Take a ticket's proof kit through its stages, from writing the cases off the ticket's Done When to QA, a Roam run, a live rehearsal, the recorded take and posting it on the PR. Use when sid types /proof-kit, or asks to write, check, QA, build, run, rehearse, record or post a ticket's proof kit. For a PR video without a kit, use pr-video.
4	argument-hint: "<ticket> [status|write|red|qa|build|check|roam|live|take|post] [flags]"
5	---
6	
7	# Proof kits for a ticket
8	
9	Invocation: `/proof-kit $ARGUMENTS`
10	
11	A proof kit is a ticket's proof written as cases before the code: the ticket
12	cases prove its Done When, QA cases cover what the change could break next
13	to it. Everything about kits is in `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/README.md`;
14	read the section a stage names before running it the first time in a session.
15	
16	Paths used below:
17	
18	- `P=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof`
19	- `K=$P/kits/eng-XXXX.json`, the kit; its `name` is `eng-XXXX`
20	- `OUT=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof`, one folder per run (`<kit>-<time>/`, with `report.md`)
21	- Run every command from `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam`, or
22	  from the worktree's `apps/roam` in a worktree session (its `node_modules` must exist).
23	
24	The stages and the flags each takes are in `stages.json` beside this file.
25	The prompt band (the `proof-kit-band` mod) shows the same list while sid
26	types `/proof-kit`, so a new stage or flag goes into `stages.json` in the
27	same session it's added to the tools.
28	
29	## Read the invocation
30	
31	The words can come in any order:
32	
33	- The kit: a ticket (`ENG-2348`, `eng-2348` or `2348` all mean the kit `eng-2348`),
34	  or a kit's own file name in `$P/kits` (`eng-2176-obsidian`, `roam-selftest`).
35	- The stage: one of the names in `stages.json`.
36	- Flags: words starting with `--`, with a value after the ones `stages.json` gives `values`.
37	  A flag that isn't listed for the stage is a mistake: say so and ask, never guess what it meant.
38	
39	## Ask for what's missing
40	
41	Sid won't remember the options, so show them when he leaves them out:
42	
43	1. **No ticket.** Take it from the session's branch or worktree name (`eng-XXXX`)
44	   when there is one. Otherwise ask with AskUserQuestion: the newest kits in
45	   `$P/kits` (by modified time, up to 3), and "Other" for a new ticket.
46	2. **No stage.** Run `status` (it only reads), then ask with AskUserQuestion:
47	   the stage `status` names as next first, marked "(Recommended)", then up to
48	   three others that fit the kit's state. Each option's description says what
49	   the stage does and whether it opens Roam.
50	3. **A stage with `presets` and no flags given.** Ask once with the presets
51	   as options, the default first. A stage without presets runs with its
52	   defaults, and the reply lists the flags it could have taken in one line.
53	
54	Never ask about something the invocation already says.
55	
56	## Stages
57	
58	**status** (reads only). No kit file: next is `write`. Otherwise run
59	`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --coverage` (cases by decision, QA areas,
60	Done When coverage; opens nothing), note `target.pr` and whether
61	`target.dist` holds an `extension.js`, and read the newest `report.md` under
62	`$OUT/eng-XXXX-*`. Next is the first of these that applies: coverage fails
63	→ `write`; no PR yet → implement (`red` first if sid wants to see the kit
64	fail); no QA areas, or cases still `proposed` → `qa`; the kit needs the
65	database and the dist is missing or older than the PR's head → `build`;
66	approved cases with only an `intent` → `write` (script their steps; the
67	kits test fails while any remain), or `live` when the path can't be read
68	from the code; otherwise `take`, then `post`.
69	
70	**write** (code only). Read the ticket with the Linear MCP (`get_issue`).
71	Read the README's "The kit", "cases", "prepare", "needs" and "Done When"
72	sections, and model the kit on `kits/eng-2348.json` (needs the database) or
73	`kits/roam-selftest.json` (UI only); recipes are in `$P/recipes/`.
74	- At least one case per Done When bullet, its `proves` naming the bullet
75	  (`"Done When 2: <the bullet's words>"`).
76	- Every approved case gets `steps`, or is a check made only of `expect.js`,
77	  before the stage ends: recipes, command palette labels exactly as registered,
78	  selectors from the code, and fixtures for the data it needs (node types,
79	  pages, relation types, settings). Don't leave a case with only an `intent`:
80	  `$P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` requires every shipped kit to be ready for an
81	  unattended take, so one intent-only case fails it for every session. When a
82	  path truly can't be read from the code, ask sid instead.
83	- Cases in Obsidian go in their own kit, `kits/eng-XXXX-obsidian.json`
84	  (`target.app: "obsidian"`; model it on `kits/eng-2195.json`), with steps
85	  from the `proof.obsidian` helpers and Obsidian's command palette. A Roam
86	  kit's page and its live rehearsal can't drive Obsidian. Each kit covers
87	  the Done When bullets it can prove in its own app.
88	- `expect.js` when code can tell (the `proof.*` helpers), `expect.text`
89	  when a person judges.
90	- `title`, `claim` and `given` in plain words, because the panel and the HUD explain the run with them.
91	- `baseline: "dg-baseline@2"` (sync and node sharing off), and
92	  `target: { "slot": "3", "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-XXXX" }` plus
93	  `"pr": <n>` once the PR exists.
94	- `needs: ["supabase", "embed-stub"]`, with its own fixtures turning sync or
95	  node sharing on, only when the feature reads or writes the database
96	  (`dg-baseline@1` still turns both on, for older kits). A kit without it
97	  runs from a shared Roam link on the PR's CI build, for anyone.
98	- When updating a kit, keep case ids and decisions as they are.
99	
100	Finish with `--coverage` passing for each kit, and
101	`pnpm exec tsx --test $P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` passing.
102	
103	**red** (opens Roam, optional). This proves the kit fails before the fix. It only works
104	before the PR exists (no `target.pr`) and for a kit that doesn't connect to
105	a database (main's CI build talks to production, and the runner refuses
106	it). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K --build main --title proof/eng-XXXX-main`
107	prints the page's link. Give it to sid to open and Run. A case that passes
108	on main proves nothing about the fix: rewrite it.
109	
110	**qa** (code only, plus a Sonnet call). This needs `target.pr` and a worktree on the
111	PR's branch. Run `npx tsx $P/qa.ts propose --kit $K [--base <ref>] [--model <m>]`,
112	then `npx tsx $P/qa.ts list --kit $K`. Ask about the proposed cases with
113	AskUserQuestion, one question per case and up to four per call. Each
114	question carries the case's title, area and intent, with the options
115	"Approve", "Reject: this PR doesn't reach it" and "Reject: another case
116	covers it" ("Other" takes sid's own reason). Record the answers with
117	`qa.ts decide --kit $K --approve <ids>`, then one
118	`qa.ts decide --kit $K --reject <id> --reason "<why>"` per rejection, since a reason belongs to its case.
119	Approved QA cases arrive with only an intent: script their steps the way
120	`write` says, and move the Obsidian ones (with their decision, and their area
121	from `surface`) into the Obsidian kit. Finish with the kits test passing.
122	
123	**build** (code only). Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --build`. It needs `target.pr`,
124	`target.dist` and a worktree at the PR's pushed head. It bakes in the proof
125	database and the embeddings stub when the kit needs them.
126	
127	**check** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database and the stub first (below). Then
128	`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --check [--slot n]`.
129	
130	**roam** (opens Roam). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K [--replace]` prints the link;
131	nothing else is needed beforehand, even for a database kit. The page's
132	checklist does the rest: **Connect this machine** starts the proof database,
133	the stub and the keys server through the `dg-proof://` handler (set up on
134	sid's machine; another developer runs `pnpm helper setup --dg <checkout>`
135	once in roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner), the PR's
136	CI build is pointed at the proof database in the browser, **Set up and load**
137	applies the graph setup, and **Ask your agent** opens an agent on by-hand
138	cases. Push refuses a page that already has a kit. `--replace` deletes that
139	kit's block, its runs log and any edits made on the page (the panel edits
140	the page), and nothing pulls page edits back into the JSON yet. Ask before
141	replacing.
142	
143	Push waits 120 s for Roam to save and can give up on a long page (a
144	186-block page took 144 s). The unsaved writes stay in the slot's profile, so
145	open the page again with `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts probe --js "<expr>"`, wait
146	until `.rm-sync__icon` has `rm-sync--synced`, and count the page's `case::`
147	blocks against the kit. For a database kit, connect this machine yourself so
148	the checklist starts at ✓: `sh ~/.local/share/dg-proof/open.sh 'dg-proof://connect'`
149	runs what the Connect button runs, and `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8766/status` should
150	report the database. Then give sid the link. Only one session drives the
151	slot's Roam window at a time, so don't push while another session is in a
152	Roam stage.
153	
154	**live** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first.
155	Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --live [flags]` in the background with a
156	log. Tell sid to watch workspace 9 and steer from the HUD; pressing Stop twice
157	ends it. After it ends, compare `diff -u $K <run folder>/kit.proposed.json`,
158	summarize what the rehearsal added, and ask whether to keep it (copy it over the kit).
159	
160	**take** (opens Roam, records). A take refuses cases that are only an intent, js
161	nobody allowed and cases still waiting for a decision. Rehearse those with
162	`live` first. In the ticket's implementation session, hand the take to a
163	subagent (Sonnet) with the exact command; elsewhere, run it here. For a
164	database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first. Run
165	`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K [flags]` in the background with a log and a
166	timeout. The run folder holds `report.md` and the video. Check the video as
167	pr-video's "Verify before sharing" says.
168	
169	**post** (outward). Show sid the report and ask before posting anything.
170	Post the report with
171	`gh api repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/issues/<pr>/comments -F body=@<report.md>`
172	(`gh pr edit` fails on this repo). For the video, follow pr-video's "Getting
173	the mp4 onto the PR".
174	
175	Starting the database and the stub, when the kit needs them:
176	`npx tsx $P/db.ts up`, and `python3 /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/recorder/embed-stub.py`
177	in the background (port 3210).
178	
179	## Rules
180	
181	- A stage marked `opensRoam` runs only when sid named it, or picked it in
182	  this invocation's question. Never start one on your own, and never run
183	  one as a follow-on from another stage. These stages run headed on workspace
184	  9, on slot 3 unless `--slot` says otherwise, and never against discourse-dev-graph.
185	- Tests never touch the production database. The tools refuse a kit that would
186	  connect on a CI build. Don't get around that with `--allow-*` flags or another build.
187	- No screenshots. The commands report text.
188	- Runs that take minutes (`live`, `take`, `qa propose`) go in the background
189	  with a log, and you report progress from the log.
190	- End every stage with what it produced (paths, the link, counts) and one
191	  line naming the next stage.
192	----
193	# Proof kits
194	
195	Proof-driven development: write the proof before the feature. A proof kit
196	holds everything one PR's proof needs, written out ahead:
197	
198	- what must be running (the proof database, the embeddings stub, the PR's build),
199	- the data to prepare, each piece with a check so prepared data is skipped,
200	- the cases and what counts as working, including cases Claude proposed from
201	  the PR's diff for the areas next to the change, each approved or rejected
202	  with the reason kept,
203	- the captions for the video.
204	
205	`prove.ts` runs a kit. It checks the needs, prepares only what's missing,
206	then records the narrated video (the default) or rehearses it live in front
207	of you. The report and the video are the PR's proof. When the data is
208	already in place, a run starts in seconds, so a kit is as easy to rerun and
209	share as a video.
210	
211	## Run a kit
212	
213	From `discourse-graph/apps/roam` (for its tsx and playwright):
214	
215	```bash
216	PROVE="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/prove.ts"
217	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --coverage   # the kit against its Done When; opens nothing
218	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --check   # what's missing, changes nothing
219	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json           # record the video
220	$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --live    # rehearse it with you
221	```
222	
223	- `--coverage` validates the kit and prints its cases by decision and its
224	  Done When coverage, without a browser, a build or the database, so a
225	  session writing code can check a kit it just wrote. `--check` opens a
226	  Roam session to look at the before-load data.
227	- `/proof-kit <ticket> [stage] [flags]` (the `proof-kit` Claude skill) walks
228	  a ticket through these commands; its stages and flags are in
229	  `~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/stages.json`, which the
230	  `proof-kit-band` mod shows above the prompt while you type the command.
231	- `--kits a.json,b.json` runs several kits one after another with the same
232	  flags and prints where each report and video landed. A failed kit doesn't
233	  stop the rest.
234	- Kits run on slot 3 (test-3-graph). discourse-dev-graph is refused unless
235	  you pass `--allow-dev-graph`.
236	- A kit that touches a database needs the proof database up (see below):
237	  `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts up`. Runs read its
238	  keys from `proof/db/.env`; `SUPABASE_*` exported in your shell are ignored.
239	- Every run writes `output/proof/<kit>-<timestamp>/`: `journal.jsonl` (every
240	  event), `report.md` (ready to post as a PR comment), plus the video, or the
241	  proposed kit and the footage for a rehearsal.
242	- Other flags (`--dist`, `--slot`, `--url`, `--allow-login`,
243	  `--allow-stale-build`, `--no-narrate`, `--mode`, `--speed`, `--dwell`) are
244	  listed at the top of `prove.ts`.
245	
246	What a run does, in order:
247	
248	1. **Needs.** Each need is checked, and a failure prints the command that
249	   fixes it. The dist must have the right env baked in, and when the kit names
250	   a PR, the dist's `buildCommit` must be the PR's head.
251	2. **Outside fixtures.** Database rows and anything else done from the shell:
252	   check, apply only if missing, check again.
253	3. **Before-load fixtures.** Flags and node types, which the extension reads
254	   once at load. They run in a session without the extension, Roam gets time
255	   to sync the writes, and a fresh session confirms them.
256	4. **The session.** In-session fixtures (pages, settings Roam resets on every
257	   load) and the baseline's smoke checks run first. In a take they're trimmed
258	   off the video. Then the cases run.
259	5. **The report.**
260	
261	## The proof database
262	
263	Kits never touch the hosted (production) database, and no longer share the
264	stack you develop against either. They get their own local Supabase:
265	
266	- **Native, no Docker.** It runs on the Supabase CLI's experimental stack
267	  (`[experimental] stack = true`), pinned to 2.119.0 in `proof/db/package.json`
268	  and installed there on first use. Its data lives in `~/.supabase/stacks/`.
269	- **Its own ports.** The API is `127.0.0.1:55321`, Postgres `55322` (the
270	  checkout's 543xx moved to 553xx), so it runs beside main's Docker stack on
271	  54321 and any worktree's. Analytics, mail and edge functions stay off.
272	  `core/database.ts` holds the address; every path in proof uses it.
273	- **A checkout's schema.** `db.ts up` writes `proof/db/supabase/` from
274	  `discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase` (config, migrations, schemas)
275	  and brings the database to those migrations: new ones apply in place, and
276	  when one it applied changed or is gone (switching from a PR's worktree back
277	  to main) it resets. `--from <worktree>` tests a PR's own migrations.
278	- **Seeded with what kits name.** The dev graph (space 66566) and the
279	  Obsidian test vault (106039) as publish sources, test-3-graph (120237), each
280	  with its anonymous account, the authors 3 and 106041, and the
281	  `eng-2329-demo` group all three are in. Generated ids start at 200000.
282	
283	```bash
284	DB="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts"
285	$DB up [--from <checkout>]   # start, migrate, seed, write proof/db/.env
286	$DB status                   # answering? which checkout's schema?
287	$DB reset                    # back to the migrations, seeded again
288	$DB sql "select id, url from \"Space\""
289	$DB stop                     # data stays for the next up
290	```

292	Builds for kits (`prove.ts --build`) bake in the proof database and the
293	embeddings stub, or no database at all when it isn't set up and the kit
294	doesn't need one. They never inherit a dev stack's env or fall back to
295	discoursegraphs.com's API.
296	
297	## Done When: the cases against the ticket
298	
299	Each case says which of the ticket's Done When bullets it covers, in
300	`proves`: by number (`"Done When 2: Enabling Stored Relations removes the
301	warning."`) or by quoting the bullet. Every run reads the ticket from Linear
302	(`LINEAR_API_KEY`) and prints each bullet with the cases that cover it.
303	`--check` fails when a bullet has no case, a number is past the last bullet,
304	or a numbered case's words read like a different bullet (the ticket's bullets
305	moved, or the kit counted wrong). A take report opens with the bullets, each
306	checked when every case under it passed, then the other cases.
307	
308	- The ticket is the kit's `ticket` (`"ENG-2348"`), else the `eng-####` in the
309	  kit's name, else in its PR's branch. Without a key or a ticket the run says
310	  so and goes on.
311	- A `proves` that names no bullet ("case 1's result, shown on screen") is
312	  fine: the case is listed as not tied to a Done When. QA cases usually are.
313	- Only approved cases count; a rejected case covers nothing.
314	
315	## QA: what else the change could break
316	
317	A kit's own cases prove the ticket. `qa.ts` covers what the change could break
318	next to it: Claude reads the PR's diff, lists the areas it reaches, and
319	proposes cases a person can test by hand. Someone approves or rejects each one.
320	A rejected case stays in the kit with its reason, so the record shows what was
321	left out and why. Approved cases run like any other case: by hand in a live
322	rehearsal or the in-Roam runner, and unattended in a take once a rehearsal has
323	written their steps.
324	
325	```bash
326	QA="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/qa.ts"
327	$QA propose --kit kits/eng-2348.json     # areas + proposed cases, from the PR's diff
328	$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json      # asks about each proposed case: approve, reject (with why), skip
329	$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json --approve <ids> --reject <ids> --reason "<why>"
330	$QA list --kit kits/eng-2348.json        # areas, and every case by decision
331	```
332	
333	- `propose` needs the PR's worktree (found from `target.pr`, or `--worktree`)
334	  and the `claude` CLI. It diffs the worktree against where it left
335	  `origin/main` (`--base` to change), and Claude (Sonnet unless `--model`)
336	  may only read files there. The diff, the prompt and the answer are kept in
337	  `output/proof/<kit>-qa-<time>/`. Run it again after a push: areas and cases
338	  the kit already has, rejected ones included, aren't proposed again.
339	- `decide` records who decided (`git config user.name`, or `--by`) and when.
340	  Each answer is saved as it's given.
341	- A take refuses while any case is still proposed. A live rehearsal and the
342	  in-Roam runner play the approved cases and say how many wait or were
343	  rejected.
344	- Reports list the rejected cases with their reasons, the cases still
345	  waiting, and each area with the approved cases that cover it.

347	## The kit
348	
349	```json
350	{
351	  "name": "eng-2348",
352	  "title": "Warn when sharing or importing with Stored Relations off",
353	  "baseline": "dg-baseline@1",
354	  "target": { "slot": "3", "pr": 1506, "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-2348" },
355	  "needs": ["supabase", "embed-stub"],
356	  "prepare": [
357	    {
358	      "id": "stored-relations-off",
359	      "why": "Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for",
360	      "phase": "in-session",
361	      "check": { "js": "..." },
362	      "apply": { "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Open - Discourse settings" }, "why": "open settings" }] }
363	    }
364	  ],
365	  "cases": [
366	    {
367	      "id": "share-warning",
368	      "title": "Share warns when Stored Relations is off",
369	      "caption": "Sharing with Stored Relations off now warns before anything leaves the graph.",
370	      "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Discover shared nodes" }, "why": "open import the way a user would" }],
371	      "expect": { "js": "if (!document.body.innerText.includes('Stored Relations')) throw new Error('No warning.')" }
372	    }
373	  ]
374	}
375	```
376	
377	### needs
378	
379	`"supabase"` (the proof database answers on 127.0.0.1:55321), `"embed-stub"` (the
380	stub answers on 127.0.0.1:3210) and `"env:NAME"` are built in. A custom need
381	is `{ "id", "why", "check": "<shell, exit 0 when met>", "fix": "<what to run>" }`.
382	Needs the kit implies are added on its own: a `rest` or `sql` fixture needs
383	Supabase and the service key, and every `{{env.NAME}}` needs `NAME`.
384	
385	### prepare
386	
387	Each fixture is `{ id, why, phase, check?, apply, settleMs? }`.
388	
389	| phase | when it runs | check | apply |
390	|---|---|---|---|
391	| `outside` | before any browser | `{ "command" }` (exit 0 = present) or `{ "rest": { "path", "expect": "rows" \| "none" } }` | `{ "command" }`, `{ "sql" }` (psql into the proof database) or `{ "rest": { "method", "path", "body?" } }` |
392	| `before-load` | in a session without the extension | `{ "js" }`, truthy = present | `{ "js" }` |
393	| `in-session` | once the extension loads, before the cases | `{ "js" }` | `{ "js" }`, or `{ "steps" }` for things only the UI can set |
394	
395	- js checks and applies are expressions, like a `js` step. Use an async IIFE
396	  for several statements.
397	- A fixture without a check runs every time. Use that for settings Roam resets
398	  on each load.
399	- `rest` reaches the proof database's REST API with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
400	- `{ "publish": { space, author, group, types, nodes } }` (outside) writes
401	  what another space's publish would have: node types (`{ id, label, format,
402	  template? }`), nodes (`{ id, type, title, body? }`) with their Document and
403	  direct and full Content rows, and ResourceAccess for the group. The
404	  space's platform picks the shapes Roam or Obsidian write. It's all upserts,
405	  so leave out the check and it runs on every take. test-3-graph is in the
406	  `eng-2329-demo` group with the dev graph (space 66566, author 3) and the
407	  Obsidian test vault (space 106039, author 106041), so either can be the
408	  source.
409	- The proof database runs without edge functions, so a Roam kit that touches
410	  the database signs in before load: the `database-session` fixture in the
411	  shipped kits runs `proof.supabase.signIn({ serviceKey, publishableKey })`.
412	  It makes what create-space would have (the graph's Space row, its
413	  anonymous account with the password the graph stores, PlatformAccount and
414	  editor access) and writes the session the extension reads. Its check,
415	  `proof.supabase.signedIn()`, asks the proof database whether it knows the
416	  session's user, so a session from another stack (DG keys every local one
417	  `sb-127:`) or from before a reset signs in again.
418	- Name what a kit creates with `{{ns}}` (the kit's namespace) so cleanup can
419	  find it and kits don't collide in a shared test graph.
420	
421	### cases
422	
423	- `steps`: recordDemo actions, each with a one-line `why`. `source` says who
424	  wrote a step: `kit`, `model` or `you`. js from `model` or `you` runs only
425	  after you allow it on the HUD, which sets `approved: true`.
426	- `intent`: plain language. A case with only an intent needs a live rehearsal,
427	  where the brain works out its steps.
428	- `expect.js` runs in the page; throwing fails the case. `expect.text` needs
429	  your eyes: you give the verdict live, and in a take the video is the
430	  evidence. A case can be only an `expect.js` check.
431	- `proves` names the Done When bullet the case covers (see "Done When"
432	  above); `checks` says in plain words what its `expect.js` checks.
433	- `decision` is `{ status: proposed | approved | rejected, by, at, reason }`.
434	  A case without one was written by hand and counts as approved; only
435	  approved cases run, and a rejected case needs its `reason`. `surface` names
436	  the area (from the kit's `surface` list) a case checks. `qa.ts` writes both.
437	- `caption` and `toast` are for the take: the narration line and the
438	  top-right flash. Write captions the way the pr-video skill says.
439	- `{ "when": { "js", "do": [actions] } }` runs its actions only when the js
440	  is truthy, so a toggle (the Discourse context overlay, say) can be turned
441	  on without turning it off on the next run. Its js counts as js for the
442	  Allow rule.
443	
444	### templates
445	
446	Any string can use `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{kit}}`, `{{run}}` and `{{ns}}`. They're
447	filled only when the string runs, so keys never land in a kit, a proposed
448	kit or a generated storyboard on disk.

450	## Obsidian kits
451	
452	A kit with `target.app: "obsidian"` (plus `vault`, `cdp`, `pr` and `dist`)
453	attaches over CDP to an Obsidian you started on the test vault with
454	`--remote-debugging-port=9223`, and records through `recordObsidian.ts`.
455	Takes and `--check` only; live rehearsals drive Roam. No baseline and no
456	before-load fixtures, since the app is already running. `--build` builds
457	apps/obsidian in the PR's worktree with the local database and the stub,
458	stages it in `dist` with `build-commit.txt`, and installs `main.js` and
459	`styles.css` in the vault, keeping the replaced files as `*.pre-<kit>`. A
460	take rebuilds and reinstalls when the vault runs another kit's build, and
461	reloads the plugin before anything else. `proof.obsidian` has the vault
462	helpers: `nodeType`, `importedFiles`, `removeNodeTypes`, `open`, `write`,
463	`setTemplates`, `notices`, `closeModals`. The palette action types into
464	Obsidian's palette.

466	## Take: the video
467	
468	The default. It needs nobody at the screen, so it refuses a kit with
469	intent-only cases, js you haven't allowed, or cases still waiting for a
470	decision, and says which. It writes a
471	small storyboard module that builds the storyboard from the kit when
472	recordDemo loads it, then runs `recorder/recordDemo.ts --narrate --cursor`
473	unchanged. Fixtures and smoke checks go in the storyboard's `setup`, which
474	recordDemo runs before scene 1 and trims off the video. The report marks each
475	case pass, fail, shown (checked by eye, see the video) or not run, with the
476	time it starts in the video (`video 1:05`), and says when setup or the video
477	assembly failed instead. The recorder logs each scene's start in the finished
478	video and embeds them as chapters in the mp4, so a player can jump from case
479	to case.
480	
481	## Live: a rehearsal you steer
482	
483	`--live` runs the kit in front of you on workspace 9. Steps the kit knows
484	replay through recordDemo's `runAction` with no model involved. A case written
485	only as an intent, a failed step, or something you ask for in chat goes to the
486	brain: a Claude Code session, ideally on Haiku, told to read this file. What
487	works is baked into `kit.proposed.json`. Review it with `diff -u`, and move it
488	over the kit to keep it. The rehearsal's report gives each case's time in the
489	session footage (`footage 4:10`), so a by-hand test has its place in the
490	recording. The session stays open after the last case so you can
491	add cases, and ends when you press Stop twice on the HUD or the brain sends
492	`stop`.
493	
494	### The HUD
495	
496	A panel in the bottom-right corner (⇆ moves it left), in a closed shadow root
497	that page scripts and Playwright selectors can't reach. While a step runs it
498	stays on screen but lets every click through.
499	
500	- At the top, what the kit proves (`claim`) and the setup it starts from
501	  (`given`). Then every case with ✓, ✗ or ▶, what it proves (`proves`), and
502	  for the current case its steps with the running one highlighted and what it
503	  checks at the end (`checks`). Write those four fields in plain words; they
504	  are what the panel has to explain the run with.
505	- A feed of what just happened: steps, checks with their failure reason,
506	  what you said and what the agent answered.
507	- Pause or Resume, Next (one step, or skip the hold), − and + for speed
508	  (0.25× to 4×), and the mode (auto, step, case).
509	- ✓ Pass and ✗ Fail: the verdict a case waits for, or end the current case
510	  early when you spot a bug.
511	- Allow or Deny: the only way js the agent wrote can run.
512	- The ask box: what you type goes to the agent as a `said` event, and its
513	  answer comes back into the feed. The dot is green while an agent is
514	  listening; with none, what you type is saved as a note.
515	- Ctrl+Alt+Space pauses or resumes; Ctrl+Alt+. runs the next step.
516	
517	### The brain's loop
518	
519	```bash
520	CTL="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/ctl.ts"
521	$CTL status
522	$CTL events '{"since":0,"waitMs":20000}'
523	$CTL steps - < steps.json
524	```
525	
526	Run it from `discourse-graph/apps/roam`. Wait for `PROOF READY` in the
527	runner's output, then long-poll `events` with the last `seq` you saw:
528	
529	| Event | What to do |
530	|---|---|
531	| `need-steps` | Read `intent`, `expect` and `aria` (the page as an aria snapshot). Send steps: `{"caseId":"...","steps":[...]}`. |
532	| `step-failed` | Read `error` and `aria`. Send a fix with `"how":"replace-failed"`, or `retry`, `skip-step`, or ask sid. |
533	| `need-approval` | Tell sid what the js does and that it waits on the HUD. You can't approve it. |
534	| `need-verdict` | Optionally check with `aria`, `text` or `query`, then propose `{"verdict":"pass","reason":"..."}`. Sid decides. |
535	| `case-end`, `cases-done` | Summarize briefly. After `cases-done`, ask whether to add cases or stop. |
536	| `session-end` | Report the paths the runner printed. |
537	| `said` | sid typed this in the panel. Do what it asks with the commands below, then answer in one or two plain sentences with `reply {"text":"..."}`. Questions ("why did it click that?") get a `reply` only. |
538	
539	When sid talks, in the panel's ask box (a `said` event) or in your chat:
540	
541	- "pause", "faster", "next", "step mode": `pause`, `speed {"speed":2}`,
542	  `next`, `mode {"mode":"step"}`.
543	- "do X instead": `pause`, write the steps, send them with
544	  `"how":"insert-next"` or `"replace-rest"` and `"by":"you"`, then `resume`.
545	- "why are you doing that?": `status` has the current step's `why` and `source`.
546	- "also test X": `add-case` with `{"by":"you","case":{"title":"...","intent":"..."}}`.
547	- A remark worth keeping: `note` with `{"text":"...","by":"you"}`.
548	
549	Writing steps: prefer clicks, typing and the command palette over js (they're
550	visible and need no Allow). Selectors are Playwright selectors; take names from
551	the aria snapshot instead of guessing. Read-only commands run freely: `aria`,
552	`text`, `query` (Datalog for `roamAlphaAPI.q`), `screenshot`, `console`. The
553	engine README's Roam pitfalls apply: click a Blueprint checkbox's
554	`.bp3-control-indicator`, match command palette labels exactly.
555	
556	Never point a kit at discourse-dev-graph, kill the runner, or type
557	credentials. If the profile is logged out, stop and hand it to sid.

559	## In Roam: kits on pages
560	
561	A kit can also live on a Roam page and run from there, with no terminal: you
562	share the page's link, whoever opens it gets the PR's build and the kit in
563	the right sidebar, and Run plays every case in their own browser. The runner
564	is the proof-runner prototype in DiscourseGraphs/roam-prototypes, a Roam
565	developer extension anyone loads once per graph:
566	
567	> Settings > Roam Depot > Developer extensions (developer mode on) > Load from URL >
568	> `https://discoursegraphs.com/releases/prototypes/previews/proof-runner/proof-runner/`
569	
570	(That's PR #26's preview; the stable `…/prototypes/proof-runner/` exists once
571	it merges, and `roam/links.ts` names the one in use.) The first block on
572	every kit page says this, for a visitor without the runner; once the runner
573	is on, that block hides. The prototype's README has the roam/js loader for
574	graphs that use that instead.
575	
576	What opening a kit page does:
577	
578	1. The runner reads the page's `{{proof}}` block: `build:: <branch>` names a
579	   CI build on Vercel Blob (the files `discoursegraphs.com/releases/roam/<branch>/`
580	   serves), `pr:: <n>` looks the branch up on GitHub.
581	2. The panel opens with a checklist of what the kit needs before Run, one
582	   line per need that applies: the runner, this machine (for a kit that
583	   needs the database), the graph setup, the build, the database session,
584	   and the agent (for by-hand cases). A met line is ✓; one that isn't shows
585	   the one button that meets it. When every line is met they fold into one,
586	   and Run is one press.
587	3. It checks the kit's before-load fixtures (baseline included). When any
588	   would change the graph, the checklist lists what will change and waits
589	   for **Set up and load**; otherwise the build loads straight away. A
590	   fixture needing a `{{env.X}}` key the browser doesn't have is skipped
591	   with a note.
592	4. A kit that needs a database (or turns on sync or node sharing) runs on
593	   the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database: before the build runs,
594	   the runner swaps its Supabase URL and key for the proof database's and
595	   DG's website API for the embeddings stub, and refuses a build where
596	   anything of the hosted stack is left. The keys come from this machine's
597	   helper; until it answers, the checklist offers **Connect this machine**
598	   (see below).
599	5. It loads the build and checks the commit inside `extension.js` against the
600	   PR's head (the CDN can lag an upload by a minute). Loaded as an extension,
601	   the runner hands the build its own `extensionAPI` (settings under `dg:`);
602	   from roam/js the build gets a stand-in that keeps settings in the browser.
603	6. The kit block opens pinned at the top of the right sidebar with the run
604	   panel: the HUD's layout, its controls, verdict buttons and feed. During a
605	   run the panel shows the page's own case blocks (Roam's `renderBlock`), not
606	   a copy: the case running now is open with its steps, the others show
607	   their `case::` line with a verdict and note beside it. Editing a step in
608	   the panel edits the page. Every rendering of a case block, in the panel
609	   and on the page, gets a colored edge for its verdict; the step running
610	   now is tinted and the steps done are dimmed.
611	7. Run plays in-session fixtures and baseline smoke checks, then the cases.
612	   A case with only an `intent` is done by hand: the panel says what to do
613	   and waits for Done, then the check or your verdict; or **Ask your agent**
614	   writes its steps (see below). A finished run adds a
615	   line to the block's `runs` list: verdicts, build and commit, time, who.
616	8. A run keeps the kit it started with. The one exception: when a step
617	   fails, fix its block in the panel and press Retry, and the fixed step
618	   runs (as the kit's own, without an Allow). Every other edit applies from
619	   the next Run.
620	
621	One build per tab: a tab that has loaded none loads a kit page's build when
622	you navigate to it, and a tab with a different build offers "Reload with
623	this build". A run that stops can resume from the next case after a reload.
624	If DG is already running (installed from Roam Depot), the runner doesn't load
625	a second copy and says so.

628	
629	- `proof/core/`: the browser-clean shared core (kit validation, machine,
630	  recipes, fixtures-to-steps, template, journal, helpers, action types). The
631	  Node files (`kit.ts`, `machine.ts`, …) re-export it and add file and shell
632	  work.

639	  `roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner/`, and runs that repo's build. The

644	
645	A kit page reads like a manual test script. Steps are sentences; the action
646	sits folded under each one.
647	
648	```
649	{{proof}} Warn when sharing with Stored Relations off
650	  kit:: eng-2348
651	  pr:: 1506
652	  baseline:: dg-baseline@1
653	  prepare
654	    Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for
655	      ```json {"id": "stored-relations-off", "phase": "in-session", ...}```
656	  case:: Discover shared nodes warns while Stored Relations is off
657	    id:: import-warns
658	    open import the way a user would
659	      use:: discover.open
660	    expect js:: `proof.waitFor(() => proof.callout('Stored relations are disabled'))`
661	  case:: Search keeps working
662	    intent:: run Node Search for "PK baseline" and look at the results
663	    expect:: the baseline nodes show and no sync error appears
664	  case:: Overlay counts stay right
665	    intent:: open a node with relations and hover the overlay
666	    area:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
667	    decision:: rejected
668	    decided by:: sid
669	    reason:: the overlay isn't touched by this PR's code path
670	  surface
671	    Discourse context overlay
672	      id:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
673	      why:: it reads the relation cache the diff changes
674	      files:: `src/cache.ts`
675	```

677	An action is `use:: <recipe>` (plus `with:: {json}`), `<kind>:: <value>` for
678	any action kind (`palette::` for command_palette), or a code block:
679	` ```javascript ` for js, ` ```json ` for any action. Put values in inline
680	code so Roam leaves brackets alone. Plain blocks under the root are notes. An
681	attribute the parser doesn't know is an error, so a typo can't leave a case
682	without its check.
