699	`run --set-up` presses Set up and load for kits that ask. Releases are cached
700	for a day and Roam loads URL extensions through the browser cache, so after
701	publishing a new runner pass `--clear-cache` (or hard-reload by hand). `install` and
702	`uninstall` put or remove the prototype's roam/js loader on `proof/runner`.
703	`push` and the other commands wait for Roam's sync icon to settle before
704	closing, since a closed tab drops writes that haven't reached the server.
705	`kits/roam-selftest.json` checks the runner itself: build load, palette,
706	Escape on a dialog, a recipe, a fixture and a by-hand case, with sync and
707	sharing off. The Playwright harness's developer-extension loader removes
708	every developer extension in the slot, the runner's too; add it back with
709	`load-url` after a take.
710	
711	### How it differs from Playwright
712	
713	- Input is made in the page: clicks wait for the target to be visible,
714	  enabled, still and not covered (the error names what covers it), keys carry
715	  `keyCode`/`which` so Blueprint dialogs close on Escape, and typing goes
716	  through `insertText`. Selectors understand the Playwright forms kits use:
717	  `:has-text()`, `:text()`, `:visible`, `>> nth=N`, `text=`.
718	- `command_palette` runs the registered command by label; the palette UI is
719	  the fallback.
720	- `screenshot` steps are skipped, and `open` only follows hash routes.
721	- CI builds are compiled against the production database, and tests never
722	  run there. A kit that needs a database, or has (or turns on) sync or node
723	  sharing, runs on the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database in the
724	  browser (step 4 above), on the machine that has the proof database. No
725	  local build is needed. Kits that only exercise UI run on CI builds as
726	  they are, for anyone: `dg-baseline@2` turns sync and node sharing off,
727	  where `dg-baseline@1` turned them on (and so needed the database).
728	
729	### This machine: Connect
730	
731	The checklist's **Connect this machine** opens a `dg-proof://connect`
732	link, which the proof helper on the machine answers: it brings up the
733	embeddings stub and the proof database when they're down, then answers on
734	`127.0.0.1:8766` with the proof database's address and the kits' env (the
735	runner fills `{{env.SUPABASE_*}}` from it, in that tab only). The panel waits
736	for it, then carries on loading. The machine line's **Disconnect** stops
737	the helper and what it started. Chrome asks once before roamresearch.com may
738	open the link and reach localhost; allow both.
739	
740	The helper is `proof/helper/` (database, stub, server, link handler, CLI),
741	and `roam/build.ts` ships it with the runner in roam-prototypes, so any
742	developer sets a machine up once, from their roam-prototypes checkout:
743	
744	```bash
745	cd roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner     # Node 22 or later
746	pnpm helper setup --dg <their discourse-graph checkout>   # --runtime docker|native, --workdir <dir>
747	```
748	
749	Setup remembers the checkout (whose migrations make the schema), runs
750	Supabase in Docker when Docker answers (natively otherwise), keeps the
751	database's files in `~/.local/share/dg-proof/db` (macOS: `~/Library/Application
752	Support/dg-proof/db`, Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dg-proof\db`), and registers
753	`dg-proof://` links: xdg on Linux, a small AppleScript app on macOS, registry
754	keys under the user on Windows (Docker only there). `pnpm helper start | stop |
755	status | uninstall` do the rest by hand. The prototype's README, "Getting set
756	up", is the developer's guide. This machine runs the source here instead, through tsx and
757	the proof database at `proof/db`:
758	
759	```bash
760	npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/helper/cli.ts setup --dg /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph --runtime native --workdir /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db
761	```
762	
763	The handler's log is `~/.local/share/dg-proof/handler.log`.
764	
765	### Your agent: Roam's MCP
766	
767	When Roam has its AI API (`extensionAPI.ai.addTool`), the runner registers
768	tools an agent connected to the graph (Roam's MCP, through a Local API
769	token) can call: `proof_status` (the cases, the checklist, where a run
770	stands), `proof_snapshot` (the page, its dialogs and their controls, for
771	selectors), `proof_control` (run, pause, resume, next, retry, skip, stop),
772	`proof_add_steps` (steps for the case waiting on them, written under the
773	case's block and run) and `proof_fix_step` (the failed step's block
774	rewritten and run). Js an agent writes waits for an Allow in the panel, and
775	verdicts are the person's. The checklist's **Ask your agent** opens a
776	`dg-proof://agent` link: the handler opens a kitty window with `claude` told
777	which kit to drive (the prompt also goes on the clipboard, for an agent
778	that's already open). The tools work where Roam's Local API reaches the
779	page, which is the Roam desktop app.
780	
781	## Safety
782	
783	- The control socket is a Unix socket in a 0700 directory with a fixed command
784	  list: no TCP port and no Node-side eval.
785	- Only the HUD can approve js or give a final verdict, and it only accepts calls
786	  with the per-session nonce from the page's main frame.
787	- Steps from the socket can't `open` another origin, and `screenshot` names
788	  can't contain slashes. Fixtures come only from the kit file, never the socket.
789	- The proof helper binds to 127.0.0.1, answers only roamresearch.com
790	  (others get 403): `GET /status` hands out the proof database's address
791	  and the kits' env (Supabase's stock keys for a stack that holds only test
792	  data) and `POST /stop` stops it. Disconnect when you're done.
793	- `dg-proof://` links carry nothing the handler runs: `connect` takes no
794	  arguments, and `agent` takes a graph name and a block uid it checks, and
795	  hands the agent its prompt through the environment, never a shell.
796	- A PR build pointed at the proof database is checked after the swap: if any
797	  hosted Supabase URL, hosted key or DG website API is left, it doesn't run.
798	- In Roam, a kit page's js runs without an Allow: whoever can edit the graph
799	  can run code for whoever presses Run, the same trust roam/js already asks
800	  for. Keep kit graphs to the team. The loader only fetches builds from DG's
801	  blob store, where only PRs from the repo itself upload, and runs the exact
802	  text whose commit the panel shows. Keys set with `setSecret` stay in that
803	  browser's storage and never go into the graph.
804	
805	## Tests
806	
807	From `discourse-graph/apps/roam`:
808	
809	```bash
810	pnpm exec tsx --test /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/__tests__/*.test.ts
811	```
812	
813	They use fakes and a headless test page. `db-live.test.ts` also signs a
814	stand-in graph in to the proof database from a page served as
815	roamresearch.com, and skips when the database isn't up. None of them open Roam;
816	`roam/cli.ts run` with `kits/roam-selftest.json` is the live check for the
817	in-Roam runner.
818

file.content:
---
name: proof-kit
description: Take a ticket's proof kit through its stages, from writing the cases off the ticket's Done When to QA, a Roam run, a live rehearsal, the recorded take and posting it on the PR. Use when sid types /proof-kit, or asks to write, check, QA, build, run, rehearse, record or post a ticket's proof kit. For a PR video without a kit, use pr-video.
argument-hint: "<ticket> [status|write|red|qa|build|check|roam|live|take|post] [flags]"
---

# Proof kits for a ticket

Invocation: `/proof-kit $ARGUMENTS`

A proof kit is a ticket's proof written as cases before the code: the ticket
cases prove its Done When, QA cases cover what the change could break next
to it. Everything about kits is in `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/README.md`;
read the section a stage names before running it the first time in a session.

Paths used below:

- `P=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof`
- `K=$P/kits/eng-XXXX.json`, the kit; its `name` is `eng-XXXX`
- `OUT=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof`, one folder per run (`<kit>-<time>/`, with `report.md`)
- Run every command from `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam`, or
  from the worktree's `apps/roam` in a worktree session (its `node_modules` must exist).

The stages and the flags each takes are in `stages.json` beside this file.
The prompt band (the `proof-kit-band` mod) shows the same list while sid
types `/proof-kit`, so a new stage or flag goes into `stages.json` in the
same session it's added to the tools.

## Read the invocation

The words can come in any order:

- The kit: a ticket (`ENG-2348`, `eng-2348` or `2348` all mean the kit `eng-2348`),
  or a kit's own file name in `$P/kits` (`eng-2176-obsidian`, `roam-selftest`).
- The stage: one of the names in `stages.json`.
- Flags: words starting with `--`, with a value after the ones `stages.json` gives `values`.
  A flag that isn't listed for the stage is a mistake: say so and ask, never guess what it meant.

## Ask for what's missing

Sid won't remember the options, so show them when he leaves them out:

1. **No ticket.** Take it from the session's branch or worktree name (`eng-XXXX`)
   when there is one. Otherwise ask with AskUserQuestion: the newest kits in
   `$P/kits` (by modified time, up to 3), and "Other" for a new ticket.
2. **No stage.** Run `status` (it only reads), then ask with AskUserQuestion:
   the stage `status` names as next first, marked "(Recommended)", then up to
   three others that fit the kit's state. Each option's description says what
   the stage does and whether it opens Roam.
3. **A stage with `presets` and no flags given.** Ask once with the presets
   as options, the default first. A stage without presets runs with its
   defaults, and the reply lists the flags it could have taken in one line.

Never ask about something the invocation already says.

## Stages

**status** (reads only). No kit file: next is `write`. Otherwise run
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --coverage` (cases by decision, QA areas,
Done When coverage; opens nothing), note `target.pr` and whether
`target.dist` holds an `extension.js`, and read the newest `report.md` under
`$OUT/eng-XXXX-*`. Next is the first of these that applies: coverage fails
→ `write`; no PR yet → implement (`red` first if sid wants to see the kit
fail); no QA areas, or cases still `proposed` → `qa`; the kit needs the
database and the dist is missing or older than the PR's head → `build`;
approved cases with only an `intent` → `write` (script their steps; the
kits test fails while any remain), or `live` when the path can't be read
from the code; otherwise `take`, then `post`.

**write** (code only). Read the ticket with the Linear MCP (`get_issue`).
Read the README's "The kit", "cases", "prepare", "needs" and "Done When"
sections, and model the kit on `kits/eng-2348.json` (needs the database) or
`kits/roam-selftest.json` (UI only); recipes are in `$P/recipes/`.
- At least one case per Done When bullet, its `proves` naming the bullet
  (`"Done When 2: <the bullet's words>"`).
- Every approved case gets `steps`, or is a check made only of `expect.js`,
  before the stage ends: recipes, command palette labels exactly as registered,
  selectors from the code, and fixtures for the data it needs (node types,
  pages, relation types, settings). Don't leave a case with only an `intent`:
  `$P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` requires every shipped kit to be ready for an
  unattended take, so one intent-only case fails it for every session. When a
  path truly can't be read from the code, ask sid instead.
- Cases in Obsidian go in their own kit, `kits/eng-XXXX-obsidian.json`
  (`target.app: "obsidian"`; model it on `kits/eng-2195.json`), with steps
  from the `proof.obsidian` helpers and Obsidian's command palette. A Roam
  kit's page and its live rehearsal can't drive Obsidian. Each kit covers
  the Done When bullets it can prove in its own app.
- `expect.js` when code can tell (the `proof.*` helpers), `expect.text`
  when a person judges.
- `title`, `claim` and `given` in plain words, because the panel and the HUD explain the run with them.
- `baseline: "dg-baseline@2"` (sync and node sharing off), and
  `target: { "slot": "3", "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-XXXX" }` plus
  `"pr": <n>` once the PR exists.
- `needs: ["supabase", "embed-stub"]`, with its own fixtures turning sync or
  node sharing on, only when the feature reads or writes the database
  (`dg-baseline@1` still turns both on, for older kits). A kit without it
  runs from a shared Roam link on the PR's CI build, for anyone.
- When updating a kit, keep case ids and decisions as they are.

Finish with `--coverage` passing for each kit, and
`pnpm exec tsx --test $P/__tests__/kits.test.ts` passing.

**red** (opens Roam, optional). This proves the kit fails before the fix. It only works
before the PR exists (no `target.pr`) and for a kit that doesn't connect to
a database (main's CI build talks to production, and the runner refuses
it). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K --build main --title proof/eng-XXXX-main`
prints the page's link. Give it to sid to open and Run. A case that passes
on main proves nothing about the fix: rewrite it.

**qa** (code only, plus a Sonnet call). This needs `target.pr` and a worktree on the
PR's branch. Run `npx tsx $P/qa.ts propose --kit $K [--base <ref>] [--model <m>]`,
then `npx tsx $P/qa.ts list --kit $K`. Ask about the proposed cases with
AskUserQuestion, one question per case and up to four per call. Each
question carries the case's title, area and intent, with the options
"Approve", "Reject: this PR doesn't reach it" and "Reject: another case
covers it" ("Other" takes sid's own reason). Record the answers with
`qa.ts decide --kit $K --approve <ids>`, then one
`qa.ts decide --kit $K --reject <id> --reason "<why>"` per rejection, since a reason belongs to its case.
Approved QA cases arrive with only an intent: script their steps the way
`write` says, and move the Obsidian ones (with their decision, and their area
from `surface`) into the Obsidian kit. Finish with the kits test passing.

**build** (code only). Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --build`. It needs `target.pr`,
`target.dist` and a worktree at the PR's pushed head. It bakes in the proof
database and the embeddings stub when the kit needs them.

**check** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database and the stub first (below). Then
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --check [--slot n]`.

**roam** (opens Roam). `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts push --kit $K [--replace]` prints the link;
nothing else is needed beforehand, even for a database kit. The page's
checklist does the rest: **Connect this machine** starts the proof database,
the stub and the keys server through the `dg-proof://` handler (set up on
sid's machine; another developer runs `pnpm helper setup --dg <checkout>`
once in roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner), the PR's
CI build is pointed at the proof database in the browser, **Set up and load**
applies the graph setup, and **Ask your agent** opens an agent on by-hand
cases. Push refuses a page that already has a kit. `--replace` deletes that
kit's block, its runs log and any edits made on the page (the panel edits
the page), and nothing pulls page edits back into the JSON yet. Ask before
replacing.

Push waits 120 s for Roam to save and can give up on a long page (a
186-block page took 144 s). The unsaved writes stay in the slot's profile, so
open the page again with `npx tsx $P/roam/cli.ts probe --js "<expr>"`, wait
until `.rm-sync__icon` has `rm-sync--synced`, and count the page's `case::`
blocks against the kit. For a database kit, connect this machine yourself so
the checklist starts at ✓: `sh ~/.local/share/dg-proof/open.sh 'dg-proof://connect'`
runs what the Connect button runs, and `curl -s 127.0.0.1:8766/status` should
report the database. Then give sid the link. Only one session drives the
slot's Roam window at a time, so don't push while another session is in a
Roam stage.

**live** (opens Roam). For a database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first.
Run `npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K --live [flags]` in the background with a
log. Tell sid to watch workspace 9 and steer from the HUD; pressing Stop twice
ends it. After it ends, compare `diff -u $K <run folder>/kit.proposed.json`,
summarize what the rehearsal added, and ask whether to keep it (copy it over the kit).

**take** (opens Roam, records). A take refuses cases that are only an intent, js
nobody allowed and cases still waiting for a decision. Rehearse those with
`live` first. In the ticket's implementation session, hand the take to a
subagent (Sonnet) with the exact command; elsewhere, run it here. For a
database kit, start the database, the stub and the build first. Run
`npx tsx $P/prove.ts --kit $K [flags]` in the background with a log and a
timeout. The run folder holds `report.md` and the video. Check the video as
pr-video's "Verify before sharing" says.

**post** (outward). Show sid the report and ask before posting anything.
Post the report with
`gh api repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/issues/<pr>/comments -F body=@<report.md>`
(`gh pr edit` fails on this repo). For the video, follow pr-video's "Getting
the mp4 onto the PR".

Starting the database and the stub, when the kit needs them:
`npx tsx $P/db.ts up`, and `python3 /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/recorder/embed-stub.py`
in the background (port 3210).

## Rules

- A stage marked `opensRoam` runs only when sid named it, or picked it in
  this invocation's question. Never start one on your own, and never run
  one as a follow-on from another stage. These stages run headed on workspace
  9, on slot 3 unless `--slot` says otherwise, and never against discourse-dev-graph.
- Tests never touch the production database. The tools refuse a kit that would
  connect on a CI build. Don't get around that with `--allow-*` flags or another build.
- No screenshots. The commands report text.
- Runs that take minutes (`live`, `take`, `qa propose`) go in the background
  with a log, and you report progress from the log.
- End every stage with what it produced (paths, the link, counts) and one
  line naming the next stage.
----
# Proof kits

Proof-driven development: write the proof before the feature. A proof kit
holds everything one PR's proof needs, written out ahead:

- what must be running (the proof database, the embeddings stub, the PR's build),
- the data to prepare, each piece with a check so prepared data is skipped,
- the cases and what counts as working, including cases Claude proposed from
  the PR's diff for the areas next to the change, each approved or rejected
  with the reason kept,
- the captions for the video.

`prove.ts` runs a kit. It checks the needs, prepares only what's missing,
then records the narrated video (the default) or rehearses it live in front
of you. The report and the video are the PR's proof. When the data is
already in place, a run starts in seconds, so a kit is as easy to rerun and
share as a video.

## Run a kit

From `discourse-graph/apps/roam` (for its tsx and playwright):

```bash
PROVE="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/prove.ts"
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --coverage   # the kit against its Done When; opens nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --check   # what's missing, changes nothing
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json           # record the video
$PROVE --kit /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2348.json --live    # rehearse it with you
```

- `--coverage` validates the kit and prints its cases by decision and its
  Done When coverage, without a browser, a build or the database, so a
  session writing code can check a kit it just wrote. `--check` opens a
  Roam session to look at the before-load data.
- `/proof-kit <ticket> [stage] [flags]` (the `proof-kit` Claude skill) walks
  a ticket through these commands; its stages and flags are in
  `~/.claude-company/skills/proof-kit/stages.json`, which the
  `proof-kit-band` mod shows above the prompt while you type the command.
- `--kits a.json,b.json` runs several kits one after another with the same
  flags and prints where each report and video landed. A failed kit doesn't
  stop the rest.
- Kits run on slot 3 (test-3-graph). discourse-dev-graph is refused unless
  you pass `--allow-dev-graph`.
- A kit that touches a database needs the proof database up (see below):
  `npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts up`. Runs read its
  keys from `proof/db/.env`; `SUPABASE_*` exported in your shell are ignored.
- Every run writes `output/proof/<kit>-<timestamp>/`: `journal.jsonl` (every
  event), `report.md` (ready to post as a PR comment), plus the video, or the
  proposed kit and the footage for a rehearsal.
- Other flags (`--dist`, `--slot`, `--url`, `--allow-login`,
  `--allow-stale-build`, `--no-narrate`, `--mode`, `--speed`, `--dwell`) are
  listed at the top of `prove.ts`.

What a run does, in order:

1. **Needs.** Each need is checked, and a failure prints the command that
   fixes it. The dist must have the right env baked in, and when the kit names
   a PR, the dist's `buildCommit` must be the PR's head.
2. **Outside fixtures.** Database rows and anything else done from the shell:
   check, apply only if missing, check again.
3. **Before-load fixtures.** Flags and node types, which the extension reads
   once at load. They run in a session without the extension, Roam gets time
   to sync the writes, and a fresh session confirms them.
4. **The session.** In-session fixtures (pages, settings Roam resets on every
   load) and the baseline's smoke checks run first. In a take they're trimmed
   off the video. Then the cases run.
5. **The report.**

## The proof database

Kits never touch the hosted (production) database, and no longer share the
stack you develop against either. They get their own local Supabase:

- **Native, no Docker.** It runs on the Supabase CLI's experimental stack
  (`[experimental] stack = true`), pinned to 2.119.0 in `proof/db/package.json`
  and installed there on first use. Its data lives in `~/.supabase/stacks/`.
- **Its own ports.** The API is `127.0.0.1:55321`, Postgres `55322` (the
  checkout's 543xx moved to 553xx), so it runs beside main's Docker stack on
  54321 and any worktree's. Analytics, mail and edge functions stay off.
  `core/database.ts` holds the address; every path in proof uses it.
- **A checkout's schema.** `db.ts up` writes `proof/db/supabase/` from
  `discourse-graph/packages/database/supabase` (config, migrations, schemas)
  and brings the database to those migrations: new ones apply in place, and
  when one it applied changed or is gone (switching from a PR's worktree back
  to main) it resets. `--from <worktree>` tests a PR's own migrations.
- **Seeded with what kits name.** The dev graph (space 66566) and the
  Obsidian test vault (106039) as publish sources, test-3-graph (120237), each
  with its anonymous account, the authors 3 and 106041, and the
  `eng-2329-demo` group all three are in. Generated ids start at 200000.

```bash
DB="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db.ts"
$DB up [--from <checkout>]   # start, migrate, seed, write proof/db/.env
$DB status                   # answering? which checkout's schema?
$DB reset                    # back to the migrations, seeded again
$DB sql "select id, url from \"Space\""
$DB stop                     # data stays for the next up
```

Builds for kits (`prove.ts --build`) bake in the proof database and the
embeddings stub, or no database at all when it isn't set up and the kit
doesn't need one. They never inherit a dev stack's env or fall back to
discoursegraphs.com's API.

## Done When: the cases against the ticket

Each case says which of the ticket's Done When bullets it covers, in
`proves`: by number (`"Done When 2: Enabling Stored Relations removes the
warning."`) or by quoting the bullet. Every run reads the ticket from Linear
(`LINEAR_API_KEY`) and prints each bullet with the cases that cover it.
`--check` fails when a bullet has no case, a number is past the last bullet,
or a numbered case's words read like a different bullet (the ticket's bullets
moved, or the kit counted wrong). A take report opens with the bullets, each
checked when every case under it passed, then the other cases.

- The ticket is the kit's `ticket` (`"ENG-2348"`), else the `eng-####` in the
  kit's name, else in its PR's branch. Without a key or a ticket the run says
  so and goes on.
- A `proves` that names no bullet ("case 1's result, shown on screen") is
  fine: the case is listed as not tied to a Done When. QA cases usually are.
- Only approved cases count; a rejected case covers nothing.

## QA: what else the change could break

A kit's own cases prove the ticket. `qa.ts` covers what the change could break
next to it: Claude reads the PR's diff, lists the areas it reaches, and
proposes cases a person can test by hand. Someone approves or rejects each one.
A rejected case stays in the kit with its reason, so the record shows what was
left out and why. Approved cases run like any other case: by hand in a live
rehearsal or the in-Roam runner, and unattended in a take once a rehearsal has
written their steps.

```bash
QA="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/qa.ts"
$QA propose --kit kits/eng-2348.json     # areas + proposed cases, from the PR's diff
$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json      # asks about each proposed case: approve, reject (with why), skip
$QA decide --kit kits/eng-2348.json --approve <ids> --reject <ids> --reason "<why>"
$QA list --kit kits/eng-2348.json        # areas, and every case by decision
```

- `propose` needs the PR's worktree (found from `target.pr`, or `--worktree`)
  and the `claude` CLI. It diffs the worktree against where it left
  `origin/main` (`--base` to change), and Claude (Sonnet unless `--model`)
  may only read files there. The diff, the prompt and the answer are kept in
  `output/proof/<kit>-qa-<time>/`. Run it again after a push: areas and cases
  the kit already has, rejected ones included, aren't proposed again.
- `decide` records who decided (`git config user.name`, or `--by`) and when.
  Each answer is saved as it's given.
- A take refuses while any case is still proposed. A live rehearsal and the
  in-Roam runner play the approved cases and say how many wait or were
  rejected.
- Reports list the rejected cases with their reasons, the cases still
  waiting, and each area with the approved cases that cover it.

## The kit

```json
{
  "name": "eng-2348",
  "title": "Warn when sharing or importing with Stored Relations off",
  "baseline": "dg-baseline@1",
  "target": { "slot": "3", "pr": 1506, "dist": "/mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-2348" },
  "needs": ["supabase", "embed-stub"],
  "prepare": [
    {
      "id": "stored-relations-off",
      "why": "Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for",
      "phase": "in-session",
      "check": { "js": "..." },
      "apply": { "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Open - Discourse settings" }, "why": "open settings" }] }
    }
  ],
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "share-warning",
      "title": "Share warns when Stored Relations is off",
      "caption": "Sharing with Stored Relations off now warns before anything leaves the graph.",
      "steps": [{ "do": { "command_palette": "DG: Discover shared nodes" }, "why": "open import the way a user would" }],
      "expect": { "js": "if (!document.body.innerText.includes('Stored Relations')) throw new Error('No warning.')" }
    }
  ]
}
```

### needs

`"supabase"` (the proof database answers on 127.0.0.1:55321), `"embed-stub"` (the
stub answers on 127.0.0.1:3210) and `"env:NAME"` are built in. A custom need
is `{ "id", "why", "check": "<shell, exit 0 when met>", "fix": "<what to run>" }`.
Needs the kit implies are added on its own: a `rest` or `sql` fixture needs
Supabase and the service key, and every `{{env.NAME}}` needs `NAME`.

### prepare

Each fixture is `{ id, why, phase, check?, apply, settleMs? }`.

| phase | when it runs | check | apply |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outside` | before any browser | `{ "command" }` (exit 0 = present) or `{ "rest": { "path", "expect": "rows" \| "none" } }` | `{ "command" }`, `{ "sql" }` (psql into the proof database) or `{ "rest": { "method", "path", "body?" } }` |
| `before-load` | in a session without the extension | `{ "js" }`, truthy = present | `{ "js" }` |
| `in-session` | once the extension loads, before the cases | `{ "js" }` | `{ "js" }`, or `{ "steps" }` for things only the UI can set |

- js checks and applies are expressions, like a `js` step. Use an async IIFE
  for several statements.
- A fixture without a check runs every time. Use that for settings Roam resets
  on each load.
- `rest` reaches the proof database's REST API with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- `{ "publish": { space, author, group, types, nodes } }` (outside) writes
  what another space's publish would have: node types (`{ id, label, format,
  template? }`), nodes (`{ id, type, title, body? }`) with their Document and
  direct and full Content rows, and ResourceAccess for the group. The
  space's platform picks the shapes Roam or Obsidian write. It's all upserts,
  so leave out the check and it runs on every take. test-3-graph is in the
  `eng-2329-demo` group with the dev graph (space 66566, author 3) and the
  Obsidian test vault (space 106039, author 106041), so either can be the
  source.
- The proof database runs without edge functions, so a Roam kit that touches
  the database signs in before load: the `database-session` fixture in the
  shipped kits runs `proof.supabase.signIn({ serviceKey, publishableKey })`.
  It makes what create-space would have (the graph's Space row, its
  anonymous account with the password the graph stores, PlatformAccount and
  editor access) and writes the session the extension reads. Its check,
  `proof.supabase.signedIn()`, asks the proof database whether it knows the
  session's user, so a session from another stack (DG keys every local one
  `sb-127:`) or from before a reset signs in again.
- Name what a kit creates with `{{ns}}` (the kit's namespace) so cleanup can
  find it and kits don't collide in a shared test graph.

### cases

- `steps`: recordDemo actions, each with a one-line `why`. `source` says who
  wrote a step: `kit`, `model` or `you`. js from `model` or `you` runs only
  after you allow it on the HUD, which sets `approved: true`.
- `intent`: plain language. A case with only an intent needs a live rehearsal,
  where the brain works out its steps.
- `expect.js` runs in the page; throwing fails the case. `expect.text` needs
  your eyes: you give the verdict live, and in a take the video is the
  evidence. A case can be only an `expect.js` check.
- `proves` names the Done When bullet the case covers (see "Done When"
  above); `checks` says in plain words what its `expect.js` checks.
- `decision` is `{ status: proposed | approved | rejected, by, at, reason }`.
  A case without one was written by hand and counts as approved; only
  approved cases run, and a rejected case needs its `reason`. `surface` names
  the area (from the kit's `surface` list) a case checks. `qa.ts` writes both.
- `caption` and `toast` are for the take: the narration line and the
  top-right flash. Write captions the way the pr-video skill says.
- `{ "when": { "js", "do": [actions] } }` runs its actions only when the js
  is truthy, so a toggle (the Discourse context overlay, say) can be turned
  on without turning it off on the next run. Its js counts as js for the
  Allow rule.

### templates

Any string can use `{{env.NAME}}`, `{{kit}}`, `{{run}}` and `{{ns}}`. They're
filled only when the string runs, so keys never land in a kit, a proposed
kit or a generated storyboard on disk.

## Obsidian kits

A kit with `target.app: "obsidian"` (plus `vault`, `cdp`, `pr` and `dist`)
attaches over CDP to an Obsidian you started on the test vault with
`--remote-debugging-port=9223`, and records through `recordObsidian.ts`.
Takes and `--check` only; live rehearsals drive Roam. No baseline and no
before-load fixtures, since the app is already running. `--build` builds
apps/obsidian in the PR's worktree with the local database and the stub,
stages it in `dist` with `build-commit.txt`, and installs `main.js` and
`styles.css` in the vault, keeping the replaced files as `*.pre-<kit>`. A
take rebuilds and reinstalls when the vault runs another kit's build, and
reloads the plugin before anything else. `proof.obsidian` has the vault
helpers: `nodeType`, `importedFiles`, `removeNodeTypes`, `open`, `write`,
`setTemplates`, `notices`, `closeModals`. The palette action types into
Obsidian's palette.

## Take: the video

The default. It needs nobody at the screen, so it refuses a kit with
intent-only cases, js you haven't allowed, or cases still waiting for a
decision, and says which. It writes a
small storyboard module that builds the storyboard from the kit when
recordDemo loads it, then runs `recorder/recordDemo.ts --narrate --cursor`
unchanged. Fixtures and smoke checks go in the storyboard's `setup`, which
recordDemo runs before scene 1 and trims off the video. The report marks each
case pass, fail, shown (checked by eye, see the video) or not run, with the
time it starts in the video (`video 1:05`), and says when setup or the video
assembly failed instead. The recorder logs each scene's start in the finished
video and embeds them as chapters in the mp4, so a player can jump from case
to case.

## Live: a rehearsal you steer

`--live` runs the kit in front of you on workspace 9. Steps the kit knows
replay through recordDemo's `runAction` with no model involved. A case written
only as an intent, a failed step, or something you ask for in chat goes to the
brain: a Claude Code session, ideally on Haiku, told to read this file. What
works is baked into `kit.proposed.json`. Review it with `diff -u`, and move it
over the kit to keep it. The rehearsal's report gives each case's time in the
session footage (`footage 4:10`), so a by-hand test has its place in the
recording. The session stays open after the last case so you can
add cases, and ends when you press Stop twice on the HUD or the brain sends
`stop`.

### The HUD

A panel in the bottom-right corner (⇆ moves it left), in a closed shadow root
that page scripts and Playwright selectors can't reach. While a step runs it
stays on screen but lets every click through.

- At the top, what the kit proves (`claim`) and the setup it starts from
  (`given`). Then every case with ✓, ✗ or ▶, what it proves (`proves`), and
  for the current case its steps with the running one highlighted and what it
  checks at the end (`checks`). Write those four fields in plain words; they
  are what the panel has to explain the run with.
- A feed of what just happened: steps, checks with their failure reason,
  what you said and what the agent answered.
- Pause or Resume, Next (one step, or skip the hold), − and + for speed
  (0.25× to 4×), and the mode (auto, step, case).
- ✓ Pass and ✗ Fail: the verdict a case waits for, or end the current case
  early when you spot a bug.
- Allow or Deny: the only way js the agent wrote can run.
- The ask box: what you type goes to the agent as a `said` event, and its
  answer comes back into the feed. The dot is green while an agent is
  listening; with none, what you type is saved as a note.
- Ctrl+Alt+Space pauses or resumes; Ctrl+Alt+. runs the next step.

### The brain's loop

```bash
CTL="npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/ctl.ts"
$CTL status
$CTL events '{"since":0,"waitMs":20000}'
$CTL steps - < steps.json
```

Run it from `discourse-graph/apps/roam`. Wait for `PROOF READY` in the
runner's output, then long-poll `events` with the last `seq` you saw:

| Event | What to do |
|---|---|
| `need-steps` | Read `intent`, `expect` and `aria` (the page as an aria snapshot). Send steps: `{"caseId":"...","steps":[...]}`. |
| `step-failed` | Read `error` and `aria`. Send a fix with `"how":"replace-failed"`, or `retry`, `skip-step`, or ask sid. |
| `need-approval` | Tell sid what the js does and that it waits on the HUD. You can't approve it. |
| `need-verdict` | Optionally check with `aria`, `text` or `query`, then propose `{"verdict":"pass","reason":"..."}`. Sid decides. |
| `case-end`, `cases-done` | Summarize briefly. After `cases-done`, ask whether to add cases or stop. |
| `session-end` | Report the paths the runner printed. |
| `said` | sid typed this in the panel. Do what it asks with the commands below, then answer in one or two plain sentences with `reply {"text":"..."}`. Questions ("why did it click that?") get a `reply` only. |

When sid talks, in the panel's ask box (a `said` event) or in your chat:

- "pause", "faster", "next", "step mode": `pause`, `speed {"speed":2}`,
  `next`, `mode {"mode":"step"}`.
- "do X instead": `pause`, write the steps, send them with
  `"how":"insert-next"` or `"replace-rest"` and `"by":"you"`, then `resume`.
- "why are you doing that?": `status` has the current step's `why` and `source`.
- "also test X": `add-case` with `{"by":"you","case":{"title":"...","intent":"..."}}`.
- A remark worth keeping: `note` with `{"text":"...","by":"you"}`.

Writing steps: prefer clicks, typing and the command palette over js (they're
visible and need no Allow). Selectors are Playwright selectors; take names from
the aria snapshot instead of guessing. Read-only commands run freely: `aria`,
`text`, `query` (Datalog for `roamAlphaAPI.q`), `screenshot`, `console`. The
engine README's Roam pitfalls apply: click a Blueprint checkbox's
`.bp3-control-indicator`, match command palette labels exactly.

Never point a kit at discourse-dev-graph, kill the runner, or type
credentials. If the profile is logged out, stop and hand it to sid.

## In Roam: kits on pages

A kit can also live on a Roam page and run from there, with no terminal: you
share the page's link, whoever opens it gets the PR's build and the kit in
the right sidebar, and Run plays every case in their own browser. The runner
is the proof-runner prototype in DiscourseGraphs/roam-prototypes, a Roam
developer extension anyone loads once per graph:

> Settings > Roam Depot > Developer extensions (developer mode on) > Load from URL >
> `https://discoursegraphs.com/releases/prototypes/previews/proof-runner/proof-runner/`

(That's PR #26's preview; the stable `…/prototypes/proof-runner/` exists once
it merges, and `roam/links.ts` names the one in use.) The first block on
every kit page says this, for a visitor without the runner; once the runner
is on, that block hides. The prototype's README has the roam/js loader for
graphs that use that instead.

What opening a kit page does:

1. The runner reads the page's `{{proof}}` block: `build:: <branch>` names a
   CI build on Vercel Blob (the files `discoursegraphs.com/releases/roam/<branch>/`
   serves), `pr:: <n>` looks the branch up on GitHub.
2. The panel opens with a checklist of what the kit needs before Run, one
   line per need that applies: the runner, this machine (for a kit that
   needs the database), the graph setup, the build, the database session,
   and the agent (for by-hand cases). A met line is ✓; one that isn't shows
   the one button that meets it. When every line is met they fold into one,
   and Run is one press.
3. It checks the kit's before-load fixtures (baseline included). When any
   would change the graph, the checklist lists what will change and waits
   for **Set up and load**; otherwise the build loads straight away. A
   fixture needing a `{{env.X}}` key the browser doesn't have is skipped
   with a note.
4. A kit that needs a database (or turns on sync or node sharing) runs on
   the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database: before the build runs,
   the runner swaps its Supabase URL and key for the proof database's and
   DG's website API for the embeddings stub, and refuses a build where
   anything of the hosted stack is left. The keys come from this machine's
   helper; until it answers, the checklist offers **Connect this machine**
   (see below).
5. It loads the build and checks the commit inside `extension.js` against the
   PR's head (the CDN can lag an upload by a minute). Loaded as an extension,
   the runner hands the build its own `extensionAPI` (settings under `dg:`);
   from roam/js the build gets a stand-in that keeps settings in the browser.
6. The kit block opens pinned at the top of the right sidebar with the run
   panel: the HUD's layout, its controls, verdict buttons and feed. During a
   run the panel shows the page's own case blocks (Roam's `renderBlock`), not
   a copy: the case running now is open with its steps, the others show
   their `case::` line with a verdict and note beside it. Editing a step in
   the panel edits the page. Every rendering of a case block, in the panel
   and on the page, gets a colored edge for its verdict; the step running
   now is tinted and the steps done are dimmed.
7. Run plays in-session fixtures and baseline smoke checks, then the cases.
   A case with only an `intent` is done by hand: the panel says what to do
   and waits for Done, then the check or your verdict; or **Ask your agent**
   writes its steps (see below). A finished run adds a
   line to the block's `runs` list: verdicts, build and commit, time, who.
8. A run keeps the kit it started with. The one exception: when a step
   fails, fix its block in the panel and press Retry, and the fixed step
   runs (as the kit's own, without an Allow). Every other edit applies from
   the next Run.

One build per tab: a tab that has loaded none loads a kit page's build when
you navigate to it, and a tab with a different build offers "Reload with
this build". A run that stops can resume from the next case after a reload.
If DG is already running (installed from Roam Depot), the runner doesn't load
a second copy and says so.

### Where the code lives

- `proof/core/`: the browser-clean shared core (kit validation, machine,
  recipes, fixtures-to-steps, template, journal, helpers, action types). The
  Node files (`kit.ts`, `machine.ts`, …) re-export it and add file and shell
  work.
- `proof/roam/`: the in-page runner (page format, selectors, input,
  executor, panel, build loader, entry), plus `build.ts` and `cli.ts`, which
  run in Node.
- `roam/build.ts` writes `roam/data.ts` (recipes and baselines as JSON
  imports), copies `core/`, `roam/`, the recipes, baselines and kits (as test
  fixtures, local paths stripped) into
  `roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner/`, and runs that repo's build. The
  prototype's `src/index.ts` (the `runExtension` wrapper), README and tests
  belong to the prototype.

### The page

A kit page reads like a manual test script. Steps are sentences; the action
sits folded under each one.

```
{{proof}} Warn when sharing with Stored Relations off
  kit:: eng-2348
  pr:: 1506
  baseline:: dg-baseline@1
  prepare
    Stored Relations is off, the state the warning is for
      ```json {"id": "stored-relations-off", "phase": "in-session", ...}```
  case:: Discover shared nodes warns while Stored Relations is off
    id:: import-warns
    open import the way a user would
      use:: discover.open
    expect js:: `proof.waitFor(() => proof.callout('Stored relations are disabled'))`
  case:: Search keeps working
    intent:: run Node Search for "PK baseline" and look at the results
    expect:: the baseline nodes show and no sync error appears
  case:: Overlay counts stay right
    intent:: open a node with relations and hover the overlay
    area:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
    decision:: rejected
    decided by:: sid
    reason:: the overlay isn't touched by this PR's code path
  surface
    Discourse context overlay
      id:: `s-discourse-context-overlay`
      why:: it reads the relation cache the diff changes
      files:: `src/cache.ts`
```

An action is `use:: <recipe>` (plus `with:: {json}`), `<kind>:: <value>` for
any action kind (`palette::` for command_palette), or a code block:
` ```javascript ` for js, ` ```json ` for any action. Put values in inline
code so Roam leaves brackets alone. Plain blocks under the root are notes. An
attribute the parser doesn't know is an error, so a typo can't leave a case
without its check.

### From a terminal

`proof/roam/cli.ts` drives the same signed-in slot profiles (slot 3 by
default), headed. From `discourse-graph/apps/roam`:

```bash
R=/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/roam/cli.ts
npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/roam/build.ts   # sync into roam-prototypes and build
npx tsx $R serve                            # serve that build on 127.0.0.1:8765, for load-url
npx tsx $R load-url --url <release dir>     # add the runner via Roam Depot's Load from URL
npx tsx $R push --kit kits/eng-2348.json    # write proof/eng-2348; prints its link (--build, --pr, --replace)
npx tsx $R run --title proof/eng-2348 --verdict pass --done   # open the link fresh, press Run, report
npx tsx $R inspect --title proof/eng-2348   # what the loader decided and what the panel says
```

`run --set-up` presses Set up and load for kits that ask. Releases are cached
for a day and Roam loads URL extensions through the browser cache, so after
publishing a new runner pass `--clear-cache` (or hard-reload by hand). `install` and
`uninstall` put or remove the prototype's roam/js loader on `proof/runner`.
`push` and the other commands wait for Roam's sync icon to settle before
closing, since a closed tab drops writes that haven't reached the server.
`kits/roam-selftest.json` checks the runner itself: build load, palette,
Escape on a dialog, a recipe, a fixture and a by-hand case, with sync and
sharing off. The Playwright harness's developer-extension loader removes
every developer extension in the slot, the runner's too; add it back with
`load-url` after a take.

### How it differs from Playwright

- Input is made in the page: clicks wait for the target to be visible,
  enabled, still and not covered (the error names what covers it), keys carry
  `keyCode`/`which` so Blueprint dialogs close on Escape, and typing goes
  through `insertText`. Selectors understand the Playwright forms kits use:
  `:has-text()`, `:text()`, `:visible`, `>> nth=N`, `text=`.
- `command_palette` runs the registered command by label; the palette UI is
  the fallback.
- `screenshot` steps are skipped, and `open` only follows hash routes.
- CI builds are compiled against the production database, and tests never
  run there. A kit that needs a database, or has (or turns on) sync or node
  sharing, runs on the PR's CI build pointed at the proof database in the
  browser (step 4 above), on the machine that has the proof database. No
  local build is needed. Kits that only exercise UI run on CI builds as
  they are, for anyone: `dg-baseline@2` turns sync and node sharing off,
  where `dg-baseline@1` turned them on (and so needed the database).

### This machine: Connect

The checklist's **Connect this machine** opens a `dg-proof://connect`
link, which the proof helper on the machine answers: it brings up the
embeddings stub and the proof database when they're down, then answers on
`127.0.0.1:8766` with the proof database's address and the kits' env (the
runner fills `{{env.SUPABASE_*}}` from it, in that tab only). The panel waits
for it, then carries on loading. The machine line's **Disconnect** stops
the helper and what it started. Chrome asks once before roamresearch.com may
open the link and reach localhost; allow both.

The helper is `proof/helper/` (database, stub, server, link handler, CLI),
and `roam/build.ts` ships it with the runner in roam-prototypes, so any
developer sets a machine up once, from their roam-prototypes checkout:

```bash
cd roam-prototypes/prototypes/proof-runner     # Node 22 or later
pnpm helper setup --dg <their discourse-graph checkout>   # --runtime docker|native, --workdir <dir>
```

Setup remembers the checkout (whose migrations make the schema), runs
Supabase in Docker when Docker answers (natively otherwise), keeps the
database's files in `~/.local/share/dg-proof/db` (macOS: `~/Library/Application
Support/dg-proof/db`, Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dg-proof\db`), and registers
`dg-proof://` links: xdg on Linux, a small AppleScript app on macOS, registry
keys under the user on Windows (Docker only there). `pnpm helper start | stop |
status | uninstall` do the rest by hand. The prototype's README, "Getting set
up", is the developer's guide. This machine runs the source here instead, through tsx and
the proof database at `proof/db`:

```bash
npx tsx /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/helper/cli.ts setup --dg /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph --runtime native --workdir /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/db
```

The handler's log is `~/.local/share/dg-proof/handler.log`.

### Your agent: Roam's MCP

When Roam has its AI API (`extensionAPI.ai.addTool`), the runner registers
tools an agent connected to the graph (Roam's MCP, through a Local API
token) can call: `proof_status` (the cases, the checklist, where a run
stands), `proof_snapshot` (the page, its dialogs and their controls, for
selectors), `proof_control` (run, pause, resume, next, retry, skip, stop),
`proof_add_steps` (steps for the case waiting on them, written under the
case's block and run) and `proof_fix_step` (the failed step's block
rewritten and run). Js an agent writes waits for an Allow in the panel, and
verdicts are the person's. The checklist's **Ask your agent** opens a
`dg-proof://agent` link: the handler opens a kitty window with `claude` told
which kit to drive (the prompt also goes on the clipboard, for an agent
that's already open). The tools work where Roam's Local API reaches the
page, which is the Roam desktop app.

## Safety

- The control socket is a Unix socket in a 0700 directory with a fixed command
  list: no TCP port and no Node-side eval.
- Only the HUD can approve js or give a final verdict, and it only accepts calls
  with the per-session nonce from the page's main frame.
- Steps from the socket can't `open` another origin, and `screenshot` names
  can't contain slashes. Fixtures come only from the kit file, never the socket.
- The proof helper binds to 127.0.0.1, answers only roamresearch.com
  (others get 403): `GET /status` hands out the proof database's address
  and the kits' env (Supabase's stock keys for a stack that holds only test
  data) and `POST /stop` stops it. Disconnect when you're done.
- `dg-proof://` links carry nothing the handler runs: `connect` takes no
  arguments, and `agent` takes a graph name and a block uid it checks, and
  hands the agent its prompt through the environment, never a shell.
- A PR build pointed at the proof database is checked after the swap: if any
  hosted Supabase URL, hosted key or DG website API is left, it doesn't run.
- In Roam, a kit page's js runs without an Allow: whoever can edit the graph
  can run code for whoever presses Run, the same trust roam/js already asks
  for. Keep kit graphs to the team. The loader only fetches builds from DG's
  blob store, where only PRs from the repo itself upload, and runs the exact
  text whose commit the panel shows. Keys set with `setSecret` stay in that
  browser's storage and never go into the graph.

## Tests

From `discourse-graph/apps/roam`:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx --test /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/__tests__/*.test.ts
```

They use fakes and a headless test page. `db-live.test.ts` also signs a
stand-in graph in to the proof database from a page served as
roamresearch.com, and skips when the database isn't up. None of them open Roam;
`roam/cli.ts run` with `kits/roam-selftest.json` is the live check for the
in-Roam runner.

--- reviews

[2026-09-30T04:36:19Z] mdroidian CHANGES_REQUESTED commit=f8e16089 id=5361530143
Could you link to the origin source (was it a block in roam?) so that we could have more context into this issue and how it relates to the issue Marc-Antoine mentioned in the comments.

Also, could you address the review comments from devin/codex?  Thanks.

--- inline
[2026-09-28T10:19:10Z] sid597 id=4121020419 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:273 commit=f8e16089
Nodes name their Source only in their title, so this scans page titles: one datalog query per published Source, and none for a publish without Source nodes. `sourceIdOfNode` then derives each candidate's source the same way publish does, which drops titles that only contain the Source title (a Claim that mentions it, or `@sun2019` inside `@sun2019direct`).

[2026-09-28T10:19:10Z] sid597 id=4121020423 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:283 commit=f8e16089
One update per published Source that has dependents. Each Source writes a different concept id, and a PostgREST update sets one value for every matched row, so they can't share a request.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020436 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:286 commit=f8e16089
This sets only `reference_content` instead of calling `upsert_concepts` again. A re-upsert would write the node's current title and edit time over its older stored body, so importers would skip its next publish. It would also insert a concept for a node this space never stored. `refs` is generated from `reference_content`, so it follows. The update needs `concept_update_policy` (space editor), which the publish upsert already needs.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020447 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:290 commit=f8e16089
The null check runs in the request, so a node that already has a source reference is never touched. `->>` returns null both for the `{}` that `omitMissingSource` stores and for a JSON null.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020453 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:501 commit=f8e16089
Obsidian repairs the same state during full sync (`findStaleSourceSlotNodeIds` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/sourceSlot.ts`). Roam's sync has no stale-slot check, so Roam repairs it when the Source is published. Once the reference exists, #1473 (ENG-2293) imports the Source with the node.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020463 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:502 commit=f8e16089
The Source's concept id comes from this publish's own `upsert_concepts` response, so there's no extra read. A Source whose upsert failed isn't in `upsertedNodeUids` and restores nothing. `conceptId !== undefined` only narrows `Map.get`: every node in the batch has a row in `upsertConcepts`.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020471 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/publishNodesToGroups.ts:523 commit=f8e16089
A failed restore reports to PostHog and doesn't fail the Source publish. The Source is still granted, and the dependent keeps its missing reference until the Source or the node is published again.

[2026-09-28T10:19:11Z] sid597 id=4121020479 reply_to=null apps/roam/src/utils/__tests__/publishNodesToGroups.test.ts:699 commit=f8e16089
`rpcCalls` staying at 2 pins that the restore doesn't re-upsert the Evidence, and the `upsertCalls` check pins that the Evidence gets no access grant. The never-stored and already-referenced cases are enforced by the update's filters, which this test asserts. The fake client can't evaluate them.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

  - `qa-only-closes-the-panel-and-keeps-focus-in`: clicks Only on Question and checks the panel is closed with focus still in the block textarea. It then types " baseline". The check is that the block reads `@PK baseline` and the menu shows only the Question result "PK baseline question".

  - `qa-select-all-label-after-only`: clicks Only on Claim and reopens the filter. It checks the header button is the blue Select all, clicks it, and checks All selected in green with every row ticked. It clicks Only on Claim again and reopens the filter. The check is that only Claim is ticked and the button is the blue Select all.
  - `qa-long-type-name-beside-the-only-button`: hovers the long-named row. A step asserts Only is visible, inside the row, narrower than 100px, uncovered, and the name does not overflow. It clicks Only. The check is that the filter closes and "No matches found" shows, because that type has no results.
  - `qa-only-works-in-a-reference-item-and`: adds the sidebar scratch page to the right sidebar through `rightSidebar.addWindow`, types `@PK` and runs the same Only checks (size and edge, then only Claim results).   **1. The kit**
  
  Kit: /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/kits/eng-2329.json. No Obsidian kit is needed.
  
  Header:
  - Database kit with `needs: ["supabase","embed-stub"]`.
  - `target` is slot 3, PR 1493, dist /mnt/data/projects/dg-test-eng-2329, viewport 1280x720.
  - It has `title`, `claim` and `given`.
  - It uses no baseline (see the first open question for why).
  
  Fixtures:
  - `database-session`: copied exactly from eng-2348.
  - `sharing-on-sync-off` (before-load): node sharing on and sync off. Sync is off so a background sync can't store the nodes before they are published. Node sharing alone still registers "DG: Share current node".
  - `evidence-and-source-types` (before-load): ensures the default Evidence format `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}` and Source `@{content}`. It only applies when they are missing.
  - `nothing-published-yet` (outside, sql, no check, so it runs every take): deletes ResourceAccess, Content, Document and Concept rows for the five fixed uids in space 120237. This makes the Evidence-before-Source order repeatable.
  - `pk-2329-pages` (in-session): pages with fixed uids.
    - `@PK 2329 source`
    - Evidence A and B, `[[EVD]] - PK 2329 evidence A/B - [[@PK 2329 source]]`
    - Evidence C, naming `@PK 2329 orphan source`
    - `@PK 2329 orphan source`

  - `evidence-first-no-reference`: publishes Evidence A through "DG: Share current node", the group switch `eng-2329-demo` and the Publish button. It checks over REST that A's concept exists with no `sourceDocument`. Its `proves` names no Done When bullet (it is the starting state of the order).
  - `source-after-evidence-restores`: publishes the Source alone. It checks A's `reference_content.sourceDocument` equals the Source concept's id. Proves "Done When 1 and 4".
  - `source-grants-no-other-node`: an `expect.js`-only check. B and C have no Concept, Content or ResourceAccess row, and only the Source and A have access rows. Proves Done When 2.
  - `missing-source-warns`: publishes Evidence C. It checks the toast contains "is not in this space yet" and that C is stored with no `sourceDocument`. It also has an `expect.text` for the toast wording. Proves Done When 3.
  
  **2. Coverage and readiness**
  
  Coverage:
  - Kit eng-2329: 14 cases, 4 approved, 10 proposed, 0 rejected, 7 QA areas.
  - ok 1. Publishing Evidence, then its Source, stores the Evidence's source reference (covered by `source-after-evidence-restores`).
  - ok 2. Publishing a Source does not publish or grant access to any other node (covered by `source-grants-no-other-node`).
  - ok 3. Publishing Evidence whose Source is not in this space still shows the missing-source warning (covered by `missing-source-warns`).
  - ok 4. Unit tests cover the Evidence-then-Source publish order (covered by `source-after-evidence-restores`).
  
  Readiness: `ready.ts` shows only the "10 proposed cases wait for a decision" blocker.
  
  **3. QA proposals**
  
  QA run folder: /mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof/eng-2329-qa-2026-10-05T07-11-16-462Z. All proposals are Roam; none needs Obsidian.
  
  | Case id | Title | Area (surface id) | Intent | My view |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `qa-source-publish-with-several-evidence` | Source publish with several Evidence restores all of them | none, so it is not tied to an area | Publish A and B before the Source, then publish the Source alone | Approve. It is cheap, since B can be published in the same flow, and it exercises the per-Source update. |
  | `qa-evidence-that-already-has-a-source` | Evidence that already has a source reference keeps it | s-evidence-already-linked-to-a-source (Evidence already linked to a Source) | Publish the Source, then Evidence A, then the Source again | Approve. It exercises the null filter on `reference_content`. |
  | `qa-unpublished-edits-to-evidence-are-not` | Unpublished edits are not published by the restore | s-evidence-published-later-with-edits (Evidence published later with edits) | Publish A, edit its body, publish the Source | Approve. It covers the review concern. The body is checked in Content. |
  | `qa-a-later-normal-publish-of-the-edited` | A later normal publish of the edited Evidence still goes through | s-evidence-published-later-with-edits | After the previous case, republish A | Reject, another case covers it. The restore does not change the publish path. |
  | `qa-evidence-for-an-unpublished-source-stays` | Evidence for an unpublished Source stays untouched | s-source-reference-on-other-evidence (Source reference on other Evidence) | Publish C, then publish the first Source | Reject, another case covers it. Evidence C already shows this in `source-grants-no-other-node` and `missing-source-warns`. |
  | `qa-pages-that-only-mention-the-source-title` | Pages that only mention the Source title are not changed | s-source-reference-on-other-evidence | Create a Claim and a page whose titles contain the Source title, then publish the Source | Approve. It exercises the substring scan, and the PR code filters with `sourceIdOfNode`. |
  | `qa-publishing-only-a-claim-runs-no-restore` | Publishing only a Claim runs no restore and no error | s-publish-of-non-source-nodes-claims (Publish of non-Source nodes) | Publish a single Claim | Reject, this PR doesn't reach it. The restore runs only when a Source is in the batch, so a Claim's publish is unchanged. |
  | `qa-source-published-together-with-its` | Source published together with its Evidence in one batch | s-publish-nodes-to-a-group-export-dialog (Publish nodes to a group) | Select the Source and A and publish together | Approve. `omitMissingSource` keeps the reference when the Source is in the same batch. |
  | `qa-source-whose-title-is-also-part-of` | Source whose title is part of another Source's title | s-source-reference-on-other-evidence | Create `Smith 2020` and `Smith 2020 appendix`, Evidence naming only the longer one, publish both | Approve. It exercises the substring-collision case, which the PR code handles through `sourceIdOfNode`. |
  | `qa-publish-a-source-after-renaming-the` | Publish a Source after renaming the Source node type | s-source-node-type-naming-and-settings (Source node type naming) | Rename the Source type, then publish it after its Evidence | Approve, but with low confidence.   - The restore deliberately updates only `reference_content`. It does not change the node's last-modified time.

  - A fresh import of the restored Evidence would work. `refreshImportedNode` has the same skip ("already up to date").
  - The PR's own Done When bullet is fine, but this is a real hole for his flow.
  
  The bots' review points are also real in the code:
  - Devin: the dependents' source is derived from the live Roam title, not the stored one. A renamed but unpublished Evidence gets the new Source's reference.
  - Devin: `findDiscourseNode` caches by uid and ignores the supplied title, so a stale cached node type can skip a candidate.
  - Codex raises the same stored-title versus live-title concern.
  
  I did not script a failing case for these, because the cases would need a rename flow plus the caching state.
  
  **5. Open questions, each with a proposed default**
  
  - Why there is no baseline: `dg-baseline@1` turns sync on, and a full sync could store the Source and Evidence before the publish, which would hide the bug. `dg-baseline@2` sets sharing off, and a kit fixture turning it on would fail the fresh-session confirm. My default is no baseline, with its own flag and node-type fixtures. Please confirm that is acceptable for a database kit.
  - The import half of Done When 1 cannot run in one graph. Discovery excludes the graph's own space, so test-3-graph can't import its own publish, and the Obsidian vault can't publish Roam nodes. Default: the Roam case proves the stored reference, and the "Importing that Evidence" sentence stays with the unit tests and ENG-2293's import tests. Do you want a second case that imports into a different slot or graph?
  - Done When 4 (unit tests) is tied to `source-after-evidence-restores` as a live equivalent. The unit tests themselves run in CI, not in Roam. Default: post the vitest result for `publishNodesToGroups.test.ts` on the PR next to the kit report.
  - Should an approved QA case exercise Marc-Antoine's re-import skip? That would need an "import, then publish the Source, then re-import" flow across two graphs. Default: no, and treat the skip as a PR finding for Sid to decide on (for example, whether the restore should bump the modified time).
  
  I did not run `qa.ts decide`.

# MANDATORY RULES — Check every session

## NEVER add Co-Authored-By
Never add `Co-Authored-By` lines to commits. All commits are sid's. No exceptions.

## NEVER cd out of the worktree
When the env says `Primary working directory: .../.claude/worktrees/<TICKET>`, all commands stay inside it. Bash cwd persists, and absolute `Edit` paths to `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/...` silently target the MAIN repo on `main`. Use `git -C <worktree>` or `(cd ...; cmd)` subshells; never bare `cd` to the main repo path. See [[feedback_stay_in_worktree]].

## NEVER use git reset --hard
`git reset --hard` destroys untracked files that were accidentally staged in a prior commit.
Use `git restore` or `git checkout -- <file>` for targeted resets. If you absolutely must
reset, stash or back up untracked files first. NEVER run `git reset --hard` without asking.

## Ticket is the spec, code is the source of truth
The Linear ticket (description + comments) is the spec. The code is the source of truth for current behavior. Anything neither settles goes to sid as a question with a proposed default. Never read Roam design blocks, worklog pages, or other upstream traces to fill a gap unless sid names the UID in this conversation, even if a launcher or memory lists them as "read first". See [[feedback-ticket-is-spec-code-is-truth]].

## NEVER assume, ALWAYS look up
When the user references something by name ("accessors", "the helper", "that util", etc.):
1. **STOP. Do NOT assume you know what they mean from conversation context.**
2. **Search the codebase** (Grep/Glob) for the actual thing they're referencing.
3. Only proceed after you've read the actual code.

This applies especially when the user says "we already have X for that" — go find X before writing anything.

## ALWAYS run all three checks after changes
From `apps/roam/` (or worktree equivalent):
1. `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <changed-files>`
2. `npx prettier --check <changed-files>`
3. `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`

All three must pass. Don't skip `tsc` — example/test files reference exported types and will break on schema changes.

## PR workflow skills (2026-08-31, supersedes the michael-trio rule)
The old trio (/think-like-michael, /review-like-michael, /save-from-myself) is SUPERSEDED — /pre-pr-review covers them. Do not run the trio per PR anymore. Standing set:

**Per PR:**
1. `/pre-pr-review` — independent Opus pass, after push and after follow-up pushes (implementer self-review doesn't count)
2. `scope-check` — after review; produces the `## Scope check` section for the PR body (team template `.github/pull_request_template.md`)
3. `pr-video` — only if the PR is missing a demo for the template's Loom section

**During implementation:** `roam-global-tailwind` when styling Roam UI.
**Team-facing prose:** `dg-engineering-writing-style` always; tickets via `dg-create-engineering-ticket`.
**Never** use `ask-as-sid` on this project.
Curt directives ("minimal commit push") still skip the per-PR skills — see [[feedback_minimal_means_skip_skills]]. Details: [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]].

## Follow findings to their conclusion
When reviewing code (especially during skill passes), if you observe facts that together imply a problem, STATE the problem. Don't list observations and move on.
- Trace return types through every call site. If a function always returns `T` (never undefined), then `?? fallback` is dead code at that site — even if other sites need it.
- "Unnecessary" = "remove it." Don't soften to "not harmful."
- "Consistent with other sites" is not a reason to keep dead code.

## Minimize reviewer cognitive load
- Don't rearrange existing code unnecessarily.
- Don't extract variables that are only used once.
- Keep diffs minimal: only change what's needed for the task.

content.text:
Each error has a different cause, and I've confirmed both.

**1. "`area::` isn't a case field": your browser is running an old copy of the proof runner.**
The runner published at the previews URL accepts `area::`, `decision::`, `decided by::`, `decided at::` and `reason::`; I downloaded it and checked its field list. The list in your error stops at `expect js`, so your tab loaded a copy from before those fields were added. Roam loads URL extensions through the browser cache, and these releases are cached for a day. All four pages will hit this, because every one has QA cases with `area::`.

To fix it, open Roam Depot > Developer Extensions and click the ⟳ refresh next to the proof-runner URL (top right in your second screenshot). A hard reload with Ctrl+Shift+R also works.

**2. "No build at …/eng-2143-…/extension.js (404)": CI has never built the Roam extension for #1412.**
- **Why there's no build:** the "PR - Roam To Blob Storage" workflow only runs when a PR's own diff touches `apps/roam/**` or the shared packages. #1412 sits on top of `eng-2143-source-adapters-base`, and its own diff is 6 files, none under `apps/roam`. So that workflow has never run for it.
- **The other pages are fine:** the CI builds for ENG-2194, ENG-2296 and ENG-2329 all return 200.
- **A build of the branch wouldn't help anyway:** it's 79 commits behind main. The Roam behaviour this kit tests (`[[@placeholder]]` and automatic source import) only exists on main.

I should have checked that each build existed before pushing the pages, and I didn't.

**Fix options for ENG-2143:**
- **Merge main into #1412 and push (recommended).** Michael's open review already needs this. Compared with its old base, the merge touches `apps/roam`, so CI uploads a build of main plus the PR's tests, and the page then loads it. First the PR's tests have to switch from `(source missing)` to `[[@placeholder]]`, or CI fails. I can do that in the eng-2143 worktree and run the checks, then show you before anything is pushed.
- **Or skip the page for ENG-2143.** Its Roam half would then run only as a terminal take on a local build.

Which do you want? Meanwhile I'm noting the build gotcha in memory so future kits check for the build first.

# Proof kits: handoff (2026-10-02)

Proof-driven development: write the proof kit first, then the feature. A kit
(`proof/kits/<name>.json`) holds needs, data preparation (each fixture with a
check), cases, and captions. `prove.ts` runs it: by default a take (the
narrated video through recordDemo), `--live` a rehearsal you steer, `--check`
a dry look, `--build` only builds and stages the PR's dist.

## Where things are

- Code: `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/proof/` (local repo, no remote).
  Commits: `f4cd177` (core) and the handoff commit after it.
- Docs: `proof/README.md` (kit format, modes, the brain's loop).
- Design page: https://claude.ai/artifact/DJpiWk9CdUDSyCwvUNnpsV (version 4).
  Part two covers proof kits, the live rehearsal, sharing, decisions and
  build order.
- recordDemo changes: exports `CURSOR_INIT_SCRIPT`, and storyboards gained
  `init` (scripts loaded in every document) and `setup` (actions before scene
  1, trimmed off the video).

## In-Roam runner (2026-10-03)

Kits run from a Roam page: share the link, whoever opens it gets the PR's
build and the kit pinned in the right sidebar, Run plays it. README section
"In Roam: kits on pages" has the page format, the code layout and the CLI.

**Rule: tests never touch the production database.** CI compiles PR builds
against production Supabase (`zytfjzqyijgagqxrzbmz`), the same one users
have. On 2026-10-03 the four v1 kits were run in Roam on CI builds with sync
on, which put test-3-graph on production (a Space row, sid's account row,
its discourse nodes and embeddings; nothing was published). That was wrong.
Sync and node sharing are off in test-3-graph again. The production rows
still need deleting by someone with production access.

### Kit pages just work: checklist, Connect, pointed builds, agent tools (built 2026-10-05)

sid's ask: opening a kit page should just work, with buttons instead of
terminal commands, the setup note at the top and only when needed, and a
way to connect his local agent through Roam's MCP.
